chunks: From him, from Al-Hajjal, from Ghalib ibn Muhammad, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).

Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Surely your Lord is in the place of watching.' He said: 'An archway upon the Bridge (Sirat), not crossed by a servant who has been unjust (to others).'

key_terms.الصِّرَاط: The Bridge over Hellfire that all must cross on Judgment Day
key_terms.المِرْصاد: The place of watching or the archway on the Sirat bridge
key_terms.مَظْلِمَةٍ: Injustice or wrong done to others (as opposed to sin against God)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'Al-Mir'sad' in Surah Al-Buruj according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (as) provides a specific eschatological interpretation of 'Al-Mir'sad' as a checkpoint on the Sirat bridge, emphasizing that divine justice is actively monitoring the transfer of rights between individuals. This highlights the Shia concept of *Haqq al-Nas* (rights of people) as a distinct barrier to salvation, requiring not just general piety but the rectification of interpersonal injustices before one can cross into Paradise.
